newsitem.title: USA: Stockbroker pleads not guilty in police killing.
newsitem.headline: Stockbroker pleads not guilty in police killing.

text.p: A New York stockbroker accused of robbing his father's penthouse and killing a police officer who blocked his escape pleaded not guilty Tuesday to first-degree murder charges.
"Not guilty, your honour," defendant Scott Schneiderman, 33, told Manhattan Supreme Court Judge Herbert Altman during his arraignment.
Schneiderman is accused of shooting Officer Anthony Sanchez, 31, last month. Sanchez's partner, relatives and three dozen officers from his precinct attended the hearing.
Schneiderman is charged with several counts of first-degree murder, second-degree murder, robbery, burglary and weapons possession.
If convicted on the first-degree murder charges, he could face the death penalty. Mayor Rudolph Guiliani is pressing law enforcement officials to seek the death penalty.
Schneiderman, a broker with D.L. Cromwell Investments, is accused of breaking into his father's penthouse apartment late on May 19. He and his father, Ray Schneiderman, are estranged.
He is alleged to have tied up his father and his girlfriend, who had summoned police, and to have taken $5,000 and a pistol from a safe.
Sanchez cornered him in a building stairwell, according to court papers. He allegedly shot Sanchez in the neck during an exchange of fire and the officer died of the wound.
Sanchez was the first New York police officer killed in the line of duty this year.
